title: Native CaseGraphen Morphism Propose Input
description: The bare CaseMorphism document `casegraphen morphism propose --input <file>` accepts. There is no case_space_id wrapper: the accepted document is the morphism itself, addressed by --case-space-id on the command line. An add/update payload of cells and relations lives at metadata.payload (added_cells, added_relations, updated_cells, updated_relations), not at the top level. Each property reuses its definition from the stored case-space contract's case_morphism record (native.case.space.schema.json#/$defs/case_morphism) by reference, but this schema's own required list is looser: added_ids, updated_ids, retired_ids, preserved_ids, violated_invariant_ids, evidence_ids, and source_ids may all be omitted here. The tool defaults every omitted one to [], and derives added_ids from metadata.payload's added_cells/added_relations when the author leaves it out. metadata stays an open object, the same as the stored contract, except for its payload key specifically: when present, payload is closed to the MorphismPayload shape (added_cells, added_relations, updated_cells, updated_relations) the CLI actually parses, so an invented key such as retired_cells fails schema validation instead of only the propose-time refusal.
